items.claim: strongest_rejected_alternative carries no rival boundary at all -- it rejects two unit_type labels -- so this six-verse span ships without engagement of any rival cut, including one its own prose points at.
items.auditor_grounds: The field rejects forcing the span into wasf_poem or narrative_sequence as a worse fit than lyric_address, and says the span is argued into lyric_address by the closest-fit operative category with the deviation disclosed below. That is a unit_type justification, and the book's operative-category law routes exactly that disclosure to device_notes, where this row already carries it -- so the rival-boundary slot is spent on a duplicate. A rival cut was available from the row's own bytes: MT 3:7-3:10 carry no first- or second-person address form at all (verified -- every suffix across those four verses is third-person), and MT 3:11 then opens צְאֶ֧ינָה וּֽרְאֶ֛ינָה בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן (oshb:Song.3.11, tier: byte), two 2fp imperatives plus the book's only daughters-of-Zion vocative (sweep: 1 verse), which under the book's voice policy is tier-1 voice-shift evidence standing exactly at the 3:10|3:11 junction. The row's own device_notes concedes the point by saying the addressee shift to the daughters of Zion only surfaces at the closing imperative in Song.3.11, and separately discloses a span-internal setumah at MT 3:8 (single-witness tier-3, correctly non-driving) at the other candidate joint. I am NOT concluding that the shipped span is wrong -- the maximal-run rule and the processional coherence support holding MT 3:6-3:11 whole -- only that the strongest available rival is unengaged, which is a warrant gap on a medium_low row. Not alone load-bearing: both outer edges stand on byte-verified tier-1 anchors. Noted inside the same sentence and folded into this finding rather than scored separately: the phrase closest-fit operative category imports governance vocabulary into row prose.
items.proposed_change: Field repair to strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the unit_type sentence with an actual rival-cut engagement -- reject, or accept and re-span, the 3:10|3:11 cut at the daughters-of-Zion vocative onset, quoting the pointed splice at oshb:Song.3.11 with its tier -- and leave the operative-category deviation disclosure where it already stands in device_notes. Any resulting respan is an adjudication question, not this review's proposal.
items.adjudicator_grounds: CONFIRM at medium (rival-engagement: a defective warrant at an internal tier-1 joint, not alone load-bearing). Re-derived both ways from the staged bytes. (1) The finding's factual ground holds. Every suffix and verb form across oshb:Song.3.6-Song.3.10 is third person: 3fs עֹלָה֙ and מְקֻטֶּ֤רֶת (oshb:Song.3.6, byte tier); 3ms/3fs מִטָּתוֹ֙ ... לָ֑הּ (oshb:Song.3.7, byte tier); 3mp/3ms כֻּלָּם֙ ... חַרְבּוֹ֙ עַל יְרֵכ֔וֹ (oshb:Song.3.8, byte tier); עָ֤שָׂה לוֹ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה (oshb:Song.3.9, byte tier); עַמּוּדָיו֙ ... רְפִידָת֣וֹ ... מֶרְכָּב֖וֹ ... תּוֹכוֹ֙ (oshb:Song.3.10, byte tier). A scan of the pointed bytes of those five verses finds no final-kaf suffix (the only final-kaf tokens are the noun הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ at MT 3:9 and בַּמֶּ֣לֶךְ at MT 3:11), no 1cs -ti perfect, no 1cp -nu form and no independent first- or second-person pronoun; the yod-final tokens are construct plurals (form claims argued from the pointed bytes plus the WEB rendering; no morphology layer is staged). Then oshb:Song.3.11 opens צְאֶ֧ינָה וּֽרְאֶ֛ינָה בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן (byte tier; WEB “Go out, you daughters of Zion, and see” web:Song.3.11): two feminine-plural imperatives plus the daughters-of-Zion vocative, which the book's voice policy lists by name among its tier-1 formula anchors (adjacent-pair sweep, skeleton tier: 1 verse, MT 3:11; the daughters-of-Jerusalem pair sweeps 7 verses at skeleton tier only because it catches the from-phrase מִבְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם at oshb:Song.3.10, byte tier, which is not an address). So a tier-1-marked rival cut stands at the 3:10|3:11 joint exactly as the finding says. (2) BOTH SIDES of that rival seam weighed from bytes. The preceding verse closes תּוֹכוֹ֙ רָצ֣וּף אַהֲבָ֔ה מִבְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Song.3.10, byte tier) with no parashah seg at MT 3:10 (the WLC inventory's segs in this span sit at MT 3:8 and MT 3:11, single-witness, tier-3; absence is never counterevidence). The following verse continues the same referent after its summons: בַּמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה ... לּ֤וֹ אִמּוֹ֙ ... וּבְי֖וֹם שִׂמְחַ֥ת לִבּֽוֹ (oshb:Song.3.11, byte tier) carries on the 3ms suffix chain of MT 3:9-3:10 and the Shelomo chain שֶׁלִּשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה (oshb:Song.3.7, byte tier) / שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה (oshb:Song.3.9, byte tier) / שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה (oshb:Song.3.11, byte tier) (Shelomo-skeleton sweep: 8 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, one of them the homograph at MT 1:7; 3 of the 8 inside this span). The governing rule that decides: the hybrid granularity permits a cut at a tier-1 marker but does not compel one, and the summons-to-view reads as the unit's own close because its object is the king the description has been building (tier-2 referential continuity, used here only to reject a cut, never to drive a seam), corroborated at tier 3 by the setumah standing AT MT 3:11 rather than at MT 3:10 (single witness). The shipped span is therefore defensible and I propose no respan. (3) The shipped row's defect is real. Its strongest_rejected_alternative rejects two unit_type labels (wasf_poem, narrative_sequence) and names no rival cut; the operative-category law routes exactly that deviation disclosure to device_notes, where the row already carries it, so the rival slot is spent on a duplicate. The row's only engagement of the 3:10|3:11 joint is the device_notes concession that the addressee shift surfaces at the closing imperative, while boundary_rationale treats a marker of the book's own tier-1 class as a unit-internal close without saying why it does not open a unit. That is an unargued warrant at the one internal joint where the book's law demands engagement: a defective warrant, medium. Not high, because both outer seams stand on tier-1 anchors weighed from both sides: front, the full adjuration הִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֜ם בְּנ֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ (oshb:Song.3.5, byte tier; setumah at MT 3:5, single-witness tier-3) closes the seek-find episode and מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר (oshb:Song.3.6, byte tier; collates byte against oshb:Song.8.5 as well; ascent-formula sweep, skeleton tier: 2 verses, MT 3:6 and MT 8:5; bare mi-zot interrogative 3 verses, MT 3:6, 6:10, 8:5) opens a fresh 3fs question; rear, MT 3:11 closes on שִׂמְחַ֥ת לִבּֽוֹ (oshb:Song.3.11, byte tier; setumah at MT 3:11, single-witness tier-3) and הִנָּ֨ךְ יָפָ֤ה רַעְיָתִי֙ (oshb:Song.4.1, byte tier) opens the his-word address, coherent with the adjacent shipped rows Song.3.5-Song.3.5 and Song.4.1-Song.4.7, which argue those same seams from their own sides. Not low: this is not a mechanical or register slip but the missing half of the row's own warrant for a six-verse span (the register bleed the auditor folded in, the governance phrase closest-fit operative category inside row prose, is a genuine low-severity component and moves the severity neither way). (4) Repair proposal tested as adversarially as the row: the field repair is byte-sound and is ENDORSED AS A PROPOSAL for owner triage, with this qualification: the replacement sentence should REJECT the 3:10|3:11 cut on the grounds in (2) (the 3ms referential chain and the Shelomo chain binding MT 3:11 to MT 3:9-3:10; the setumah at MT 3:11 disclosed single-witness, tier-3, corroboration only), quoting the pointed onset splice of oshb:Song.3.11 with its byte tier, and leave the deviation disclosure in device_notes; the accept-and-respan branch is not supported by these bytes and is not proposed. Non-span item: span_change false, span_ruling n/a; both sides of every seam in play were weighed from bytes.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The seam verse (web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1) opens a new exchange against its own front seam: oshb:Song.6.12 closes in first-person singular — לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי נַפְשִׁ֣י שָׂמַ֔תְנִי (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) — while oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13 opens with the repeated 2fs imperative summons שׁ֤וּבִי שׁ֨וּבִי֙ הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית שׁ֥וּבִי שׁ֖וּבִי (byte tier) 'return, return, the Shulammite; return, return', addressed to an epithet unique to this verse (הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית — byte sweep: 1 verse book-wide, 2 occurrences in-verse), an addressee-and-person shift of tier-1 class. The catchword נָדִֽיב (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) immediately before and בַּת נָדִ֑יב (oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, byte tier) immediately after bracket this single-verse span on both seams (skeleton sweep: 2 verses book-wide). Within the verse the summons is followed by מַֽה תֶּחֱזוּ֙ בַּשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) 'why do you gaze at the Shulammite' — WEB “Return, return, Shulammite! Return, return, that we may gaze at you. Why do you desire to gaze at the Shulammite, as at the dance of Mahanaim?” (web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1). Whether the second half is spoken by the same voice as the opening summons is argued from the bytes alone (not from the WEB [SPEAKER] heading), so the call-and-question is held as one exchange rather than split at an unmarked internal line.

items.claim: The Shulammite uniqueness citation blends two count objects: the in-verse occurrence digit it reports is false for the byte-swept token it names.
items.auditor_grounds: The row writes the epithet citation as a single byte-tier object with two digits - 1 verse book-wide and 2 occurrences in-verse. Re-swept with the object named: the byte-tier token הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13) returns 1 verse and 1 token occurrence book-wide, not 2. The verse's second epithet token is בַּשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier), a bet-prefixed form that is a different string at byte tier AND at skeleton tier, and it byte-sweeps to 1 verse / 1 token of its own. The 2-occurrence digit is true only for the prefix-tolerant epithet skeleton, which sweeps to 1 verse and 2 token occurrences. The book-wide uniqueness half of the claim is true at either object; the in-verse half is byte-false as cited. Not load-bearing: the seam rests on the fourfold 2fs imperative summons שׁ֤וּבִי שׁ֨וּבִי֙ הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית שׁ֥וּבִי שׁ֖וּבִי (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) against the 1cs close of oshb:Song.6.12, so the digit corroborates rather than drives.
items.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale only (no span effect): re-cut the parenthetical so each digit names its own object and unit - the exact byte-tier epithet token at 1 verse / 1 token book-wide, and, separately labelled, the prefix-tolerant epithet skeleton at 1 verse / 2 token occurrences in this verse, naming the bet-prefixed second token as the reason the two objects differ. Retire the blended 'byte sweep: 1 verse book-wide, 2 occurrences in-verse' formulation.
items.adjudicator_grounds: CONFIRM at medium (E-05 count-object blend: a false digit at the object named, not load-bearing). Re-derived both ways from the staged bytes. (1) The row's parenthetical names the pointed token הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) as a byte-sweep object and attaches two digits, 1 verse book-wide and 2 occurrences in-verse. Re-swept with each object named: the exact byte token הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית returns 1 verse and 1 token book-wide (in-verse byte count 1); the verse's second epithet token is the bet-prefixed בַּשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier), a different string at byte, accent-stripped and skeleton tier, itself 1 verse / 1 token; only the prefix-tolerant epithet skeleton שולמית (the consonants shared by both tokens; skeleton tier) returns 1 verse / 2 tokens. So the book-wide-uniqueness half is true at every object, while the in-verse digit is false at the byte object the row names and true only at a skeleton object the row does not name: the finding's grounds re-derive exactly, and the shipped formulation is a blended count of the class the book's count discipline forbids. (2) Not load-bearing, established by weighing the seam from both sides. The preceding verse closes in 1cs, לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי נַפְשִׁ֣י שָׂמַ֔תְנִי (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier; the exegesis note at MT 6:12 is single-witness apparatus), and the seam verse opens on the fourfold 2fs imperative summons שׁ֤וּבִי שׁ֨וּבִי֙ הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית שׁ֥וּבִי שׁ֖וּבִי (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier; imperative-token sweep, skeleton tier: 1 verse / 4 tokens, all in MT 7:1), a person-and-addressee shift of the tier-1 class (gendered verb forms argued from the pointed bytes and the WEB rendering “Return, return, Shulammite!” web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1; no morphology layer is staged). The rear seam is held on form, not voice: the seam verse closes כִּמְחֹלַ֖ת הַֽמַּחֲנָֽיִם (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) and the next verse opens the suffixed-body-part wasf מַה יָּפ֧וּ פְעָמַ֛יִךְ בַּנְּעָלִ֖ים בַּת נָדִ֑יב (oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, byte tier), while the 2fs address itself runs across the join from וְנֶחֱזֶה בָּ֑ךְ (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) into פְעָמַ֛יִךְ (oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, byte tier), exactly as the following shipped row Song.7.1-Song.7.5 argues the same seam from its side, so the two rows are coherent. The nadiv catchword straddle the row discloses re-sweeps to 2 verses at skeleton tier: נָדִֽיב (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) and בַּת נָדִ֑יב (oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, byte tier). The epithet digit decorates the addressee's uniqueness; neither seam rests on it, so the defect is a defective digit claim not alone load-bearing: medium by the severity law, not high; not low, because the claim as written is false at its named object rather than merely undigited. No parashah seg, paseq or K/Q stands at MT 7:1 (WLC inventory; absence never counterevidence). Every written dual in the row (WEB 6:13 = MT 7:1; WEB 7:1 = MT 7:2) is arithmetically right through the crosswalk, and the row's curly WEB quotation verifies verbatim at web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1. (3) Repair proposal validated as adversarially as the row: the auditor's field repair carries only digits re-derived above (exact byte token 1 verse / 1 token; prefix-tolerant skeleton 1 verse / 2 tokens, the second being the bet-prefixed form) and changes no span, so it is ENDORSED AS A PROPOSAL for owner triage, with the offset-zone dual qualifier retained on every ref it touches. Count-object item: span_change false, span_ruling n/a; both sides of the row's seams were nonetheless weighed from bytes to fix load-bearing status.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The brothers' deliberation opens with a 1cp possessive, אָח֥וֹת לָ֨נוּ֙ קְטַנָּ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.8, byte tier) 'a little sister [belongs] to us', marking a new speaker-group distinct from the woman's own 1cs voice throughout the surrounding movements (this achot token is role-split from the bride-epithet achoti used earlier in the book) — the sister here is theirs, not his address to her; the speaker-group identification itself is a content inference rather than a named form, though the keeper-and-vineyard chain at oshb:Song.1.6, בְּנֵ֧י אִמִּ֣י (byte tier), the same 'my mother's sons' phrase, links the same group across the book. WEB: “We have a little sister. She has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister...” (web:Song.8.8). The wall/door conditional in 8:9 continues the same 1cp voice — נִבְנֶ֥ה and נָצ֥וּר (oshb:Song.8.9, byte tier) — as a compact, self-contained mashal, and the immediately preceding verse (web:Song.8.7) closes under a setumah division. The row's own back seam carries a byte-true straddling device: אִם חוֹמָ֣ה הִ֔יא (oshb:Song.8.9, byte tier) is answered clause-for-clause by אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier), and וְשָׁדַ֖יִם אֵ֣ין לָ֑הּ (oshb:Song.8.8, byte tier) is answered by וְשָׁדַ֖י כַּמִּגְדָּל֑וֹת (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) — the wall-noun חוֹמָ֣ה/חוֹמָ֔ה pair is the lexeme's only two sites in the book, byte tier at each ref, identical only once cantillation is stripped (accent_stripped tier as a pair). The seam nonetheless survives the straddle because the 1cp-to-1cs person change at the oshb:Song.8.9|8.10 boundary is itself in-verse and marked, not because the wall-and-breast answer is absent.

items.claim: The exclusivity claim that the wall-noun pair is 'the lexeme's only two sites in the book' is false at the lexeme object it names: the same lexeme's defective-spelled plural stands at MT 5:7.
items.auditor_grounds: Re-swept with the object named. At the plene singular SPELLING the row quotes - חוֹמָ֣ה (oshb:Song.8.9, byte tier) and חוֹמָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) - the skeleton sweep returns exactly 2 verses (MT 8:9, MT 8:10) and 2 token occurrences, so the digit is right for that spelling. But the row names the count object as 'the lexeme', and the same lexeme's plural stands at oshb:Song.5.7 as שֹׁמְרֵ֖י הַחֹמֽוֹת (byte tier, spliced from the source bytes): written defective, without the vav, it is invisible to any plene sweep - the defective skeleton returns 1 verse (MT 5:7) while the plene plural skeleton returns 0 verses. At the lexeme object the true count is 3 verses (MT 5:7, MT 8:9, MT 8:10), so 'the lexeme's only two sites in the book' is a false exclusivity claim, and it is the book's own mater-lectionis / defective-plene hazard class realised. Not load-bearing: the row states expressly that the seam survives on the in-verse 1cp-to-1cs person change at oshb:Song.8.9|8.10, not on the straddling device the digit decorates.
items.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale only (no span effect): re-cut the count object from 'the lexeme' to the attested plene singular spelling, carry the digit as a spelling-scoped sweep (2 verses, MT 8:9 and MT 8:10), and disclose the defective plural at MT 5:7 as the third lexeme site the plene sweep does not reach. Keep the byte / accent_stripped tier labels on the pair as written - they are correct.
items.adjudicator_grounds: CONFIRM at medium (E-05 false exclusivity claim at the count object named, not load-bearing). Re-derived both ways from the staged bytes. (1) The row writes that the wall-noun pair חוֹמָ֣ה (oshb:Song.8.9, byte tier) / חוֹמָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) is the lexeme's only two sites in the book.
